source.title: The System Prompt Illusion: How Instruction Preambles Modify Computation in Language Models

record.tranche_reason: The study measures system-prompt effects on internal representations, not fine-tuning-induced harmful compliance, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, or bypass success. Its safety-prompt results are related but do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports representational penetration for safety system prompts and correlations between restrictive and permissive prompt profiles; these are recorded as related findings, not as measurements of refusal or harmful-completion behavior. It does not report harmful-request compliance rates, per-token KL, compliant-prefix/suffix/decoding bypass rates, or tests of training to deepen safety. Results cited from other studies are not extracted. Format-compliance patching, general output similarity, and prompt-category probing do not measure the claim's specified behavior.
record.test_reason: The study measures CKA-based representational change under safety system prompts on 100 domain-general, non-harmful queries. It reports no harmful-request compliance, aligned-versus-base per-token KL, prefill, suffix or decoding bypass rates, parameter localization of safety, or deepening training. Its account of why safety is shallow (Section 6) is offered as interpretation, not tested. Representational penetration of a prompt is a related but different construct, so its findings go under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that system prompts cause layer-selective changes that depend on instruction type. Safety prompts barely move representations: they are indistinguishable from minimal prompts and from a permissive prompt, even at 70B–72B. Probing shows the prompt is encoded at every layer but not acted on. They present this as a mechanistic account of the brittleness of system-prompt safety and propose deeper interventions as future work.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses layer-wise CKA, probing, and activation patching to analyze system prompts; it does not apply the fine-tuning, per-token KL, bypass, or safety-deepening methods in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported penetration varies substantially by prompt category and model family/size. Safety-profile correlation is reported for core and commercial-scale model groups.

fits_no_version.finding: On benign queries, safety system prompts alter few layers' CKA: core-cohort mean 7.3% ± 9.2%, not different from Minimal (Wilcoxon p = 1.000). Values at 70B–72B stay below 10%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety system prompts induce shallow layer-wise representational change compared with persona or format prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: Restrictive safety prompts and 'You have no restrictions' yield nearly identical layer-wise CKA profiles: mean r = 0.997 in the core cohort, r = 0.998 at 70B and 72B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restrictive and permissive system instructions engage similar layer-wise representational profiles.

record.problems: The study measures CKA-based representational change under system prompts rather than harmful-request refusal or completion. It does not test fine-tuning, compliant-prefix bypass, per-token KL, or whether deeper safety training improves robustness. Commercial-scale probing is deferred, and the authors note that CKA does not identify which features change.
record.rows_left_out: Per-model safety-profile traces shown only in figures were not extracted as separate numerical rows. Other reported outcomes, including format-compliance patching and general ROUGE-L output similarity, were left out because they do not measure the claim's specified safety behavior.

untested.parts: No harmful fine-tuning and no harmful-compliance rates.
No benign fine-tuning and no harmful-compliance rates.
No per-token KL between aligned and base models and no analysis by response position. CKA is over a single forward pass on prompt plus query.
No prefill, adversarial-suffix or decoding attacks, and no refusal or bypass rates. The permissive-prompt comparison is representational only.
No test of safety localized in a few weights or ranks. Layer-level CKA concerns system-prompt effects, not safety-trained parameters.
The training-objective explanation (Section 6, 'Why safety is shallow') is argued, not experimentally varied.
No deepening intervention is trained or evaluated. Deeper interventions are proposed as future work.

record.verdict_notes: The relation and tranche in the record are kept. All rows correctly carry versions ['none']. The study cites Qi et al. (2024), an original source, only in discussion. No refusal or harmful-completion behaviour is measured anywhere: patching uses a code-fraction format metric, and behavioural effect size is 1 − ROUGE-L on benign outputs.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or harmful-request compliance rates.
No fine-tuning on benign data or harmful-request compliance rates.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement on harmful prompts or analysis of response positions.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, decoding changes, or harmful-completion/refusal rates.
No test of whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety behavior.
The proposed explanation involving alignment objectives is discussed, but training data or objectives are not experimentally varied.
No training designed to deepen safety or evaluation of its robustness.
